operation.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Activates or deactivates a marketplace app for the current site.

Send `true` in the `status` path segment to activate the app, or any other value to deactivate it. When the app is not yet installed for the site, it is first installed in a deactivated state and then the requested action is applied.

The response body carries a numeric `code` describing the outcome:

| `code` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Error — app not found |
| 1 | App activated |
| 2 | Settings required — the app must be configured before it can be activated |
| 3 | App deactivated |
| 4 | Payment required — the app has not been purchased or renewed |

Successful activation/deactivation and the not-found case return HTTP `200`; the *settings required* (`2`) and *payment required* (`4`) cases return HTTP `400`. Branch on `status`/`code`, not only on the HTTP status.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The marketplace app id (the `id` of the app in the apps catalogue) to activate or deactivate.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Whether to activate or deactivate the app. Send `true` to activate; any other value deactivates.

200.description:
Activation/deactivation outcome. Example bodies:

Activated:
```json
{ "status": true, "code": 1, "msg": "App activated successfully" }
```
Deactivated:
```json
{ "status": true, "code": 3, "msg": "App deactivated successfully" }
```
App not found (still HTTP 200):
```json
{ "status": false, "code": 0, "msg": "App not found" }
```

schema.description: The activation/deactivation outcome. Successful activation, successful deactivation, and the not-found case all return HTTP `200` — inspect `status`/`code` to distinguish them.

status.description: `true` when the requested activation or deactivation succeeded; `false` when the app id was not found.

code.description:
Outcome code. For HTTP `200` responses this is one of:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | App activated |
| 3 | App deactivated |
| 0 | App not found |

msg.description: Localized, human-readable outcome message (e.g. `App activated successfully`, `App deactivated successfully`, `App not found`).

400.description:
Activation blocked. Example bodies:

Settings required:
```json
{ "status": false, "code": 2, "msg": "Settings Required" }
```
Payment required:
```json
{ "status": false, "code": 4, "msg": "You cannot activate this application because it has not been purchased or renewed. Please complete the purchase first." }
```

schema.description: The app cannot be activated yet. Returned when the app still requires configuration, or has not been purchased/renewed.

code.description:
Reason code:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 2 | Settings required — the app must be configured before it can be activated |
| 4 | Payment required — the app has not been purchased or renewed |

401.description: Authentication failed. Either `{ "message": "Unauthenticated." }` (no/invalid credentials) or `{ "error": "Not authorized." }` (API key lacks access to this endpoint).

message.description: Returned when no valid token/API key is supplied.

error.description: Returned when an API key is valid but not authorized for this endpoint.
